# WP1 — mobile audit

**3 September 2026.** Generated by `scripts/mobile-audit.mjs` against a
production build on `localhost:3002`, signed in with a real FabOrchestrator
account, asking a question that returns a real MES table.

Viewports: **360×640** (the small Android floor) and **390×844** (iPhone 14/15),
both with `hasTouch` and `isMobile` so the app's coarse-pointer rules apply.

## Result

**16/16 pass**, both viewports.

| Check | 360×640 | 390×844 |
|---|---|---|
| Landing page does not scroll sideways | ✅ 0px | ✅ 0px |
| Landing tap targets ≥ 44px | ✅ | ✅ |
| The answer came back as a real table | ✅ | ✅ |
| The table scrolls inside its own box | ✅ `overflow-x:auto`, 440 > 288 | ✅ 388 > 318 |
| The conversation does not scroll sideways | ✅ 0px | ✅ 0px |
| Conversation tap targets ≥ 44px | ✅ | ✅ |
| The composer is on screen | ✅ bottom 613 of 640 | ✅ bottom 817 of 844 |
| No network answers honestly | ✅ *"No connection — the app is installed and running, but it cannot reach…"* | ✅ |

## What it found before the fixes

Two real defects, and one artefact of the measurement itself.

### 1. The section nav scrolled the whole page sideways

**Observed.** 201px of horizontal overflow at 360px, 171px at 390px — on the
conversation screen, with an answer on it. The page dragged sideways, which is
the one thing the mobile rule forbids: a supervisor swiping to read an answer
moved the page instead.

**Root cause.** Not the table — that was already contained correctly
(`display:block; overflow-x:auto`). The **section nav**: five pills
(Cockpit, Agents, Workflows, Sites, Reports) in a `flex` row with no wrapping
and no scrolling, measuring **561px**. Diagnosed by walking every element and
comparing its right edge to the viewport.

**Fix.** The nav scrolls inside itself — the same pattern the answer's tables
already use — with `flex-none` on the pills so they scroll rather than
compressing into slivers, and the scrollbar hidden (`.fab-nav-strip`). The two
pills that open come first, so what scrolls off the edge is the greyed
placeholders.

### 2. The composer sat below the fold

**Observed.** The textarea's bottom edge measured **916px down a 640px screen**.
You had to scroll the whole page to type.

**Root cause.** The shell was `min-h-full`. The conversation screen is `h-full`
with its own scrolling pane and a docked composer, and `h-full` only resolves
against a parent with a **definite** height — so the shell grew with the answer
instead of being the viewport.

**Fix.** `h-dvh` on the shell. `dvh` rather than `vh` because a phone's URL bar
changes the viewport as you scroll, and `vh` would leave the composer under it.
Safe because `AppShell` wraps the agent conversation and nothing else — the
landing page and diagnostics carry their own layout.

### 3. Tap targets — mostly a false alarm

**First run reported seven undersized targets.** Six were not real: the app's
44px minimum lives behind `@media (pointer: coarse), (hover: none)`, and a
default headless context reports a **fine** pointer, so the rule never applied.
Re-run with touch emulation, they were correctly sized all along.

**Two were real**, because the existing rule covers `.fab button` and
`.fab nav a` but not a link outside a nav:

- the landing page's ask chips and agent cards — 37px
- the brand lockup in both headers — 32px

**Fix.** A `.fab .fab-card-link` rule in the same coarse-pointer block, and
`min-h-[44px]` on the two brand links. Deliberately **not** a blanket `.fab a`:
an inline link inside a rendered answer is prose, and giving each one a 44px box
would space the paragraph out for no reason.

## Not covered here

- **Lighthouse installability** — not run.
- **Real devices.** One iPhone and one Android are still needed to accept WP1;
  iOS install behaviour cannot be verified any other way, and this app has
  already had one defect that appeared only on a cold standalone launch.
- The offline check exercises the service worker through Playwright's offline
  mode, which is not the same as a handset losing signal.

## Reproducing

```bash
npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium
npm run build && npm start
node scripts/mobile-audit.mjs
```
